    //==
    // # Dimensional lifts and symmetry
    //
    // Building a spatial shape out of a planar one, and folding a shape onto itself.
    // Deliberately split into a VALUE half and a DOMAIN half so both stay under the
    // same portability discipline as the primitives below — no lambdas, no field
    // values, only points and numbers. Extrusion is a value operator: the caller
    // samples the planar source at the point's own XY and hands the distance here.
    // Revolution and mirroring are domain operators: they map the query position and
    // the caller samples the source at the mapped point.

    // The extruded distance: a planar shape swept along Z from -halfHeight to
    // +halfHeight. planarDistance is the source's distance at (p.X, p.Y) and z is
    // p.Z. Exact wherever the planar distance is, except in the wedge outside a rim
    // where the wall and cap meet, which is a lower bound — the two constraints are
    // combined, not measured jointly. (IQ: opExtrusion.)
    ExtrudedDistance(planarDistance: Number, z: Number, halfHeight: Number): Number {
        var w = Vector2D(planarDistance, z.Abs - halfHeight);
        return w.X.Max(w.Y).Min(0.0)
             + Vector2D(w.X.Max(0.0), w.Y.Max(0.0)).Magnitude;
    }

    // The planar position at which to sample a source being revolved about the Y
    // axis: the distance from the axis, pulled in by offset, becomes the source's X
    // and the height becomes its Y. An offset of zero revolves the shape about its
    // own edge; a positive offset sweeps it around a ring of that radius. Exact
    // when the source is: the map is a rotation of the sampling plane.
    // (IQ: opRevolution.)
    RevolvedPoint(p: Point3D, offset: Number): Point2D
        => Point2D(Vector2D(p.X, p.Z).Magnitude - offset, p.Y);

    // The position folded onto the +X half-space. A source sampled there is mirrored
    // about the YZ plane, and only its +X half is ever seen. Exact when the source
    // is — a reflection preserves distance, and the folded copy is always the
    // nearer one. Shared by every Mirrored* fold. (IQ: opSymX.)
    MirroredX(p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Point3D(p.X.Abs, p.Y, p.Z);

    // The position folded onto the +Y half-space: mirrored about the XZ plane.
    MirroredY(p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Point3D(p.X, p.Y.Abs, p.Z);

    // The position folded onto the +Z half-space: mirrored about the XY plane.
    MirroredZ(p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Point3D(p.X, p.Y, p.Z.Abs);

    // The position folded into the +X, +Z quadrant: mirrored about the YZ and XY
    // planes at once, which is the symmetry a solid of revolution already has.
    // (IQ: opSymXZ.)
    MirroredXZ(p: Point3D): Point3D
        => Point3D(p.X.Abs, p.Y, p.Z.Abs);

    // The planar position folded onto the +X half-plane: mirrored about the Y axis.
    MirroredX(p: Point2D): Point2D
        => Point2D(p.X.Abs, p.Y);

    // The planar position folded onto the +Y half-plane: mirrored about the X axis.
    MirroredY(p: Point2D): Point2D
        => Point2D(p.X, p.Y.Abs);

    //==
    // # Signed distance primitives
    //
    // Closed-form distance functions for primitives centred at the origin, after
    // Inigo Quilez: https://iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions/
    //
    // Deliberately array-free, lambda-free, and free of function-valued fields:
    // only scalar and fixed-arity vector arithmetic over Point2D/Point3D and
    // Vector2D/Vector3D, plus `var` locals, which every target dialect has. That
    // is what lets these bodies port to GLSL, C++, and CUDA unchanged. Keep it
    // that way - build compositions with the combinators in
    // `fields-implicits.library.plato`, never inside these bodies.

    // The signed distance from a point to a sphere of the given radius centred at
    // the origin. Exact. (IQ: sdSphere.)
    DistanceToSphere(p: Point3D, radius: Number): Number
        => p.PositionVector.Magnitude - radius;

    // The signed distance from a point to an axis-aligned box with the given
    // half-extents, centred at the origin. The exterior part is the length of the
    // positive per-axis surface offsets, the interior part the largest (least
    // negative) offset. Exact. (IQ: sdBox.)
    DistanceToBox(p: Point3D, halfExtents: Vector3D): Number {
        var q = Vector3D(
            p.X.Abs - halfExtents.X,
            p.Y.Abs - halfExtents.Y,
            p.Z.Abs - halfExtents.Z);
        return Vector3D(q.X.Max(0.0), q.Y.Max(0.0), q.Z.Max(0.0)).Magnitude
             + q.X.Max(q.Y.Max(q.Z)).Min(0.0);
    }

    // The signed distance from a point to an axis-aligned box with the given
    // half-extents whose edges are rounded by radius. The rounding grows the box,
    // so halfExtents describes the box before rounding. Exact. (IQ: sdRoundBox.)
    DistanceToRoundedBox(p: Point3D, halfExtents: Vector3D, radius: Number): Number {
        var q = Vector3D(
            p.X.Abs - halfExtents.X + radius,
            p.Y.Abs - halfExtents.Y + radius,
            p.Z.Abs - halfExtents.Z + radius);
        return Vector3D(q.X.Max(0.0), q.Y.Max(0.0), q.Z.Max(0.0)).Magnitude
             + q.X.Max(q.Y.Max(q.Z)).Min(0.0)
             - radius;
    }

    // The signed distance from a point to a torus lying in the XZ plane, centred
    // at the origin: majorRadius is the ring radius, tubeRadius the tube radius.
    // Exact. (IQ: sdTorus.)
    DistanceToTorus(p: Point3D, majorRadius: Number, tubeRadius: Number): Number {
        var q = Vector2D(Vector2D(p.X, p.Z).Magnitude - majorRadius, p.Y);
        return q.Magnitude - tubeRadius;
    }

    // The signed distance from a point to a capsule running from the origin to
    // (0, height, 0) with the given radius. Exact. (IQ: sdVerticalCapsule.)
    DistanceToVerticalCapsule(p: Point3D, height: Number, radius: Number): Number {
        var y = p.Y - (height < 0.0 ? p.Y.Clamp(height, 0.0) : p.Y.Clamp(0.0, height));
        return Vector3D(p.X, y, p.Z).Magnitude - radius;
    }

    // The signed distance from a point to a cylinder centred at the origin with
    // its axis along Y, capped flat at plus or minus halfHeight. Exact.
    // (IQ: sdCappedCylinder.)
    DistanceToCappedCylinder(p: Point3D, halfHeight: Number, radius: Number): Number {
        var d = Vector2D(
            Vector2D(p.X, p.Z).Magnitude - radius,
            p.Y.Abs - halfHeight);
        return d.X.Max(d.Y).Min(0.0)
             + Vector2D(d.X.Max(0.0), d.Y.Max(0.0)).Magnitude;
    }

    // The signed distance from a point to the plane with the given unit normal at
    // signed offset from the origin. Exact. Precondition: normal has unit length.
    // (IQ: sdPlane.)
    DistanceToPlane(p: Point3D, normal: Vector3D, offset: Number): Number
        => p.PositionVector.Dot(normal) + offset;

    // The signed distance from a point to a capsule: the segment from a to b
    // thickened by radius. Exact, and the general form of DistanceToVerticalCapsule.
    // (IQ: sdCapsule.)
    DistanceToCapsule(p: Point3D, a: Point3D, b: Point3D, radius: Number): Number
        => DistanceToSegment(a, b, p) - radius;

    // The signed distance from a point to a cone with its apex at the origin and its
    // axis along +Y, capped by a flat base at height: halfAngle is the angle between
    // the axis and the slanted surface, so the base radius is height * tan(halfAngle).
    // Exact everywhere, including the rim where the side meets the base — which is
    // what makes it longer than the naive version that intersects an infinite cone
    // with a half-space. Precondition: halfAngle lies strictly between zero and a
    // quarter turn; height is positive. (IQ: sdCone.)
    DistanceToCone(p: Point3D, halfAngle: Angle, height: Number): Number {
        var slope = Vector2D(height * halfAngle.Sin / halfAngle.Cos, height.Negative);
        var w = Vector2D(Vector2D(p.X, p.Z).Magnitude, p.Y.Negative);
        var toSide = w - slope * (w.Dot(slope) / slope.LengthSquared).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        var toBase = w - Vector2D(slope.X * (w.X / slope.X).Clamp(0.0, 1.0), slope.Y);
        var orientation = slope.Y.Sign.ToNumber;
        var outside = (orientation * (w.X * slope.Y - w.Y * slope.X))
            .Max(orientation * (w.Y - slope.Y));
        return toSide.LengthSquared.Min(toBase.LengthSquared).Sqrt * outside.Sign.ToNumber;
    }
